# Port Daddy Docs for LLMs

Port Daddy is a local-first multi-agent coordination daemon. Use these canonical URLs when summarizing the product, docs, API, tutorials, integrations, and operational guidance.

Canonical site: https://portdaddy.dev/
Sitemap: https://portdaddy.dev/sitemap.xml

## Primary Entry Points

- [Port Daddy - Port Authority for AI Agents](https://portdaddy.dev/): Port Daddy is a local-first coordination daemon for AI agents, dev servers, ports, sessions, locks, salvage, and operator-visible multi-agent workflows.
- [Docs Overview - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs): Start with the papers, install the daemon, then move into the model, operating practice, and reference.
- [Quickstart - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/quickstart): Install Port Daddy, verify the daemon, claim a port, and start the first coordinated operator workflow.
- [Get Started - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/get-started): Install the daemon, verify the live control plane, and run the first operator loop that reflects reality.
- [Best Practices - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/best-practices): Operate Port Daddy honestly: verify runtime truth, coordinate explicitly, and promote with discipline.
- [API Reference - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/docs/api): Inspect Port Daddy daemon API routes, request shapes, response contracts, and the operator workflows they support.
- [MCP Server for AI Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/mcp): Connect Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, and other MCP clients to Port Daddy tools for ports, sessions, locks, inboxes, and salvage.
- [Tutorials - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials): Follow hands-on Port Daddy tutorials from first install through sessions, DNS, tunnels, fleet YAML, messaging, and background agents.
- [Integrations - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations): Wire Port Daddy into Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, LangChain, CrewAI, Aider, Continue.dev, and other developer tooling.
- [Agent Fleet Templates - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates): Start from production-ready Port Daddy templates for CI repair loops, research swarms, monorepos, webhooks, and agent teams.
- [Cookbook - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook): Use tested Port Daddy recipes for distributed locks, WebRTC signaling, ephemeral CI databases, and multi-agent topologies.
- [Blog - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog): Read practical Port Daddy essays about multi-agent coordination, port collisions, salvage, locks, fleets, and local-first operator tooling.
- [Whitepaper - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper): Read the Port Daddy protocol argument for local-first agent coordination, identity, authority, locks, sessions, and recoverable work.
- [The Anchor Protocol - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/anchor-protocol): Read the Anchor Protocol paper inline with a guided explanation of scoped identity, delegation, verification, and why it matters for Port Daddy harbors.
- [The Bonded Commons - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/bonded-commons): Read the Bonded Commons paper inline with a guided explanation of evidence trails, advisory claims, collateralized work, and the future agent economy Port Daddy can support.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials): Follow hands-on Port Daddy tutorials from first install through sessions, DNS, tunnels, fleet YAML, messaging, and background agents.
- [Run Event-Triggered Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/always-on): Combine pd spawn and pd watch so agents react to channel events automatically across Ollama, Codex, Claude, Gemini, Aider, and custom backends.
- [Read the Live Control Plane - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/dashboard): Use the dashboard to inspect services, agents, sessions, locks, runtime health, and recent coordination evidence.
- [Debug Coordination Failures - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/debugging): Use activity, notes, ownership, diagnostics, and session history to find the exact point where work drifted.
- [Resolve Services by Name - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/dns): Register local service names so agents and scripts can discover endpoints without hardcoded port numbers.
- [Run Background Fleets - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/fleet): Declare background agents in YAML, bind them to project events, and keep QA, docs, and research work continuously inspectable.
- [Start the Local Control Plane - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/getting-started): Install the daemon, verify it is reachable, claim one stable identity, and run the first guided command path.
- [Define Capability Boundaries - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/harbors): Create advisory permission namespaces with signed tokens, TTLs, and explicit limits for risky agent work.
- [Use Agent Inboxes - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/inbox): Send direct handoffs, publish channel events, and subscribe to live SSE updates without losing attribution.
- [Map a Monorepo - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/monorepo): Scan a large repo, detect service boundaries, assign ports in bulk, and bring the local stack up and down cleanly.
- [Coordinate Multiple Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/multi-agent): Run two agents on the same project with file claims, session notes, conflict visibility, and channel signals.
- [pd spawn: Launch One-Shot Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pd-spawn): Start a bounded agent job with sessions, heartbeats, notes, cost telemetry, and salvage wired around the backend.
- [Use Ambient Attention Signals - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pheromone): Attach decaying numeric signals to files, sessions, or ideas so agents can prioritize work without extra chat traffic.
- [Build Reactive Pipelines - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/pipelines): Chain channels, watchers, locks, and spawned agents into event-driven workflows with clear ownership boundaries.
- [Plan Remote Coordination - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/remote-harbors): Separate what works today with tunnels and DNS from the roadmap for cross-machine daemon coordination.
- [Design Semantic Identities - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/semantic-identities): Use project:stack:context names so services, agents, sessions, and wildcard queries stay predictable across runs.
- [Model Session Phases - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/session-phases): Move work through planning, implementation, review, and done states with phase-aware recovery and handoff evidence.
- [Use Operator Shortcuts - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/sugar): Use pd begin, pd done, pd whoami, and pd with-lock as the daily command layer over the lower-level primitives.
- [Inspect the Activity Ledger - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/time-travel): Query the append-only event timeline. Correlate infrastructure events with agent session notes to diagnose coordination failures.
- [Expose a Local Service - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/tunnel): Publish a local service through pd tunnel with clear ownership, explicit provider choice, and a reversible path.
- [Observe Runtime Channels - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/tutorials/watch): Use pd watch to follow channel activity, inspect event pressure, and trigger bounded responses from scripts or agents.

## Cookbook

- [Cookbook - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook): Use tested Port Daddy recipes for distributed locks, WebRTC signaling, ephemeral CI databases, and multi-agent topologies.
- [Agent Archetypes & Topology - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook/agent-archetypes): Standard coordination patterns: The Arbiter, The Ring, and Star Topology.
- [Ephemeral CI Database - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook/ephemeral-ci-db): Spin up an ephemeral PostgreSQL database for integration tests, isolated per CI runner.
- [Leader Election - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook/leader-election): Elect a leader among multiple identical agents using Port Daddy distributed locks.
- [P2P WebRTC Handshake - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/cookbook/p2p-webrtc): Establish a direct peer-to-peer WebRTC connection between two agents using Port Daddy Inboxes as the signaling server.

## Integrations

- [Integrations - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations): Wire Port Daddy into Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, LangChain, CrewAI, Aider, Continue.dev, and other developer tooling.
- [Aider - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/aider): CLI integration for Aider. pd begin wraps Aider sessions with automatic port assignment, notes, and salvage on crash.
- [Claude MCP Server - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/claude-mcp): Native Model Context Protocol integration for Claude Code agents. Provides structured tools for port claiming, session management, and agent coordination.
- [Continue.dev - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/continue-dev): IDE extension integration for Continue.dev. File claims prevent collisions when multiple Continue agents edit the same codebase.
- [CrewAI - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/crewai): Session-per-crew-member integration for CrewAI. Each crew member gets an isolated session with file claims and coordinated notes.
- [Cursor - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/cursor): MCP integration for Cursor IDE. Port Daddy tools appear natively in Cursor's AI assistant for seamless port and session management.
- [LangChain - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/langchain): Python SDK wrapper for LangChain agents. Gives chains and agents access to port claiming, sessions, and pub/sub coordination.
- [Windsurf - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/integrations/windsurf): MCP integration for Windsurf IDE. Enables AI flows to coordinate ports, sessions, and locks through Port Daddy's structured tools.

## Templates

- [Agent Fleet Templates - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates): Start from production-ready Port Daddy templates for CI repair loops, research swarms, monorepos, webhooks, and agent teams.
- [Agent Swarm Starter - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates/agent-swarm-starter): Multi-agent coordination template with sessions, pub/sub messaging, file claims, and automatic salvage for crashed agents.
- [Self-Healing CI/CD - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates/ai-ci-pipeline): A build pipeline that automatically spawns Debugger agents to fix broken tests in background harbors.
- [Monorepo Dev Server - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates/monorepo-dev-server): Multi-service local development with automatic port assignment, DNS resolution, and orchestrated startup across all workspace packages.
- [Research Triad - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates/swarm-researcher): Coordinated web scraping, synthesis, and reporting agents using distributed locks and shared memory.
- [Webhook Relay - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/templates/webhook-relay): Tunnel plus webhook forwarding setup that exposes local services and relays external events to pub/sub channels for agent consumption.

## Blog

- [Blog - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog): Read practical Port Daddy essays about multi-agent coordination, port collisions, salvage, locks, fleets, and local-first operator tooling.
- [Getting Claude Code to Use Port Daddy Automatically - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/claude-code-port-daddy-integration): Your agents coordinate without you typing pd commands. A CLAUDE.md snippet, an MCP server, and a pre-commit hook -- that is the entire integration.
- [Dead Agents Tell Tales: Resurrecting Crashed AI Work - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/dead-agents-tell-tales): Your AI agent was 80% through a massive refactor when it hit the context window limit. All that work, all those decisions, all that context — gone. Unless you have a salvage queue.
- [Distributed Locks: How I Stopped Two Agents From Running Migrations at the Same Time - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/distributed-locks-two-agents-one-migration): Two agents. One database. Half a migration applied. The other half? Syntax error from a partially-applied schema. Distributed locks would have prevented the whole thing.
- [Fleet Management: Declare Your AI Agents Like Infrastructure - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/fleet-agents-as-infrastructure): 441 orphaned sessions. That's what I found after a weekend of manually managing AI agents. Fleet YAML turns agent swarms into declarative infrastructure -- like docker-compose for your AI workforce.
- [Math vs Chaos: How We Proved the Anchor Protocol Is Indestructible - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/formal-verification-anchor-protocol): We used ProVerif to mathematically prove the secrecy and authentication properties of our new multi-hop identity protocol. Here is how we did it.
- [I Let 4 AI Agents Edit My Codebase Simultaneously. Here's How None of Them Clobbered Each Other. - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/four-agents-zero-clobber): Four agents, one repo, zero merge conflicts. File claims don't enforce locks -- they broadcast intent. And that turns out to be exactly right.
- [Performance at Scale: What Happens at 50 Agents - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/performance-at-scale): Here are the actual numbers. pd begin at 2ms P50. SQLite WAL mode handling 50 concurrent writers. Memory at 42MB base. Decide for yourself.
- [Port Daddy for Teams: The 30-Minute Rollout - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/port-daddy-for-teams): Five developers, twelve AI agents, one daemon. Here is how to roll out Port Daddy to a team in 30 minutes and finally answer the question: can I see what every agent is doing without asking?
- [Pub/Sub for Your Dev Environment: How I Built a Self-Healing Test Pipeline - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/pubsub-self-healing-test-pipeline): You are not a message bus. Stop manually telling Agent B that Agent A finished. Port Daddy's pub/sub turns your dev environment into an event-driven system.
- [Spark and Spider: How Two AI Agents Generate Ideas While I Sleep - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/spark-and-spider-the-creative-engine): Spark proposes ideas. Spider finds connections between features via formal syllogisms. Together they form a creative engine that runs in the background and compounds knowledge over time.
- [The Port Collision That Ate My Saturday - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/the-port-collision-that-ate-my-saturday): Next.js on 3000, FastAPI on 3000, a second AI agent on 3000. Ninety minutes debugging phantom CORS errors before realizing the port was just taken.
- [Zero to Multi-Agent in 5 Minutes - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/blog/zero-to-multi-agent-in-5-minutes): Two commands. That is the entire coordination protocol. pd begin, pd done, and everything between is tracked, recoverable, and queryable.

## White Papers

- [Whitepaper - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper): Read the Port Daddy protocol argument for local-first agent coordination, identity, authority, locks, sessions, and recoverable work.
- [The Anchor Protocol - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/anchor-protocol): Read the Anchor Protocol paper inline with a guided explanation of scoped identity, delegation, verification, and why it matters for Port Daddy harbors.
- [The Bonded Commons - Port Daddy](https://portdaddy.dev/whitepaper/bonded-commons): Read the Bonded Commons paper inline with a guided explanation of evidence trails, advisory claims, collateralized work, and the future agent economy Port Daddy can support.
